fields.label: What this is
fields.options: AstroHQ asks the astrology API for an astrologer's charts: birth chart, dasha, panchang, KP and matching. It can ask through the hub, which passes the request on to the engine, or straight to the astrology API: the small service on this server, or an AWS Lambda function. Only the numbers the calculation needs are sent (date, time, latitude, longitude and the time zone), never a name.

fields.description: Off, AstroHQ asks the astrology engine nothing and no chart can be made.
fields.label: Charts Are Available

fields.description: Through the hub: the hub keeps count of the calls and passes each on to the engine. Straight: AstroHQ asks the astrology API itself, with the key set on that service. AISpark Services: through IntegrationHQ's AISpark Services account (the server's services, with this site's customer key); the address and key below are not used.
fields.label: How AstroHQ Reaches It
fields.options:

fields.label: AISpark Services account
fields.description: Leave empty to use the one that is connected.

The hub's address, for example https://hub.example.com, or the astrology API's, for example http://127.0.0.1:8795 for the service on this server. It must start with https:// (an address on this computer may start with http://).
fields.label: Address

fields.description: The key the hub gave to AstroHQ, or, going straight, the key set on the astrology API. It is kept encrypted and is never shown again.
fields.label: API Key

fields.description: The name the astrology API has in the hub's API Registry.
fields.label: Name of the API in the Hub

fields.description: How long to wait for an answer before giving up (5 to 60). A chart takes about a second; the first one after a quiet time can take a few.
fields.label: Wait for an Answer (seconds)
What Is Kept And What Is Shown

fields.description: The engine's answers are kept for each person so a report, a page and a second report cost no new call. An answer made before this date is asked for again: put today's date here after the engine has been updated.
fields.label: Kept Answers Are Good From

fields.description: A customer's report and page show only the sections an astrologer has checked (a section of a layout says so with "reviewed"). Tick this to show all of them to customers too, with a Draft mark: for a demonstration. Astrologers and the team always see all.
fields.label: Show Sections Nobody Has Checked To Customers

fields.options: The Panchang page and the card over the Home banner show the panchang and the chaugharia of any day and any town. Fill in the place below to switch them on; blank means they show nothing.

fields.label: Place for the Panchang
fields.description: The town shown to a visitor who has not chosen another, written as Town, State, for example Delhi, India. Blank: the Panchang is off.

fields.label: Kind of Guide the Muhurat Button Connects To
fields.description: For example Pandit ji. The button connects the visitor to a guide of this kind who is live now (a Talk now with the topic below); when none is live it opens the list of those who can be booked. Blank: no button.

fields.label: Topic Sent With the Muhurat Button
fields.description: What the visitor's booking says it is about, one of the topics a visitor can choose when booking.

fields.label: New Days Worked Out In A Minute, At Most
fields.description: A visitor may ask for any date and town. Each day and town the engine has not worked out yet takes it a fraction of a second. Over this many a minute, visitors are asked to wait a moment; days already worked out are always shown.

fields.label: Requests A Visitor May Make In A Minute
Chal in the Chaugharia Is
fields.description: Chal is good in the astrology library's own division and neutral in some books. Good: it is green with Labh, Amrit and Shubh. Neutral: it is shown as neutral, neither to choose nor to avoid. Changing it asks the engine again for the days kept.

fields.label: First Year of the Panchang
fields.description: The years the astrology service works the panchang of a day out for (its README). A date outside them is taken to the nearest end.

fields.label: Days a Day of the Default Town Is Kept
fields.description: A day worked out for the default town is kept this long, so that the first visitor of a day waits for nothing.

fields.label: Days a Day of Any Other Town Is Kept
Sunrise and Moonrise Are When
fields.description: apparent: the upper edge of the sun or the moon is on the horizon, the light bent by the air: what printed panchangs and most apps use. centre: the centre of the disc with no bending: the astrology library's own rule, about four minutes later for the sun and ten for the moon. Everything counted from sunrise (Rahu Kaal, the chaugharia) follows it. Changing it asks the engine again for the days kept.
